gr.title: Σε δύο ζώνες ο καιρός σήμερα 28η Οκτωβρίου: Πού χρειάζεται προσοχή
gr.description: Με δύο πρόσωπα ο καιρός σήμερα Τετάρτη 28 Οκτωβρίου: Στα ανατολικά και νότια τα εντονότερα φαινόμενα. Με καιρικό «διπλό πρόσωπο» θα κυλήσει φέτος η 28η Οκτωβρίου, καθώς ένα νέο κύμα κακοκαιρίας, σε συνδυασμό με ψυχρές αέριες μάζες από τα Βαλκάνια, θα επηρεάσει κυρίως την ανατολική και νότια Ελλάδα. Στα ανατολικά και τα νότια αναμένουμε βροχές, καταιγίδες, ισχυρούς βοριάδες και αισθητή πτώση της θερμοκρασίας, ενώ, παράλληλα, ελλοχεύει ο κίνδυνος τοπικών πλημμυρών σε ήδη επιβαρυνθείσες περιοχές. Στα δυτικά και τα βόρεια, πάλι, τα φαινόμενα θα είναι πιο περιορισμένα Σύμφωνα με τον μετεωρολόγο του Open Κλέαρχο Μαρουσάκη, οι μεγαλύτερες πιθανότητες για προβλήματα στις παρελάσεις εστιάζονται σε Θεσσαλία, Μαγνησία, Σποράδες, Εύβοια και ανατολική Στερεά. Στην Αττική, οι πρωινές ώρες θα είναι πιο επιβαρυμένες, κυρίως στα βόρεια και ανατολικά. Στο κέντρο της Αθήνας ενδέχεται να υπάρξουν διαστήματα ύφεσης ή μόνο ασθενής βροχή. Η θερμοκρασία την ώρα της παρέλασης θα κυμανθεί στους 13°C. Στη Θεσσαλονίκη, η εικόνα θα είναι ηπιότερη. Το νυχτερινό κύμα βροχοπτώσεων αναμένεται να υποχωρήσει το πρωί, αν και δεν αποκλείονται τοπικές βροχές στην έναρξη της στρατιωτικής παρέλασης. Ο υδράργυρος θα δείξει 13 έως 16°C. Στα Δωδεκάνησα, με επίκεντρο τη Ρόδο, αναμένονται ισχυρές και επαναλαμβανόμενες καταιγίδες από την Τρίτη έως την Πέμπτη, ενώ διακυμάνσεις θα παρουσιάσουν τα φαινόμενα σε Κυκλάδες και Κρήτη. Η θερμοκρασία θα σημειώσει πτώση, με τις μέγιστες τιμές να κυμαίνονται από 13 έως 19°C. Στο Αιγαίο και πρόσκαιρα στο βόρειο Ιόνιο οι βοριάδες θα φτάσουν τα 7 με 8 μποφόρ, εντείνοντας το κρύο. Τέλος, χιονοπτώσεις θα σημειωθούν στα ορεινά πάνω από τα 1.400 μέτρα, όπως στον Παρνασσό, τον Όλυμπο και την Πίνδο. #28Η_ΟΚΤΩΒΡΙΟΥ #ΚΑΙΡΟΣ

in.title: J&K Bank begins Vigilance Awareness Week, reaffirms commitment to integrity
in.description: Srinagar, Oct 27: Reaffirming its commitment to transparency, accountability and ethical banking, J&K Bank today commenced Vigilance Awareness Week 2026 with an Integrity Pledge ceremony at its Corporate Headquarters. The observance centres on the theme “Probity for Prosperity”. Executive Director Sudhir Gupta chaired the inaugural function and administered the pledge to the bank's leadership, including Chief General Managers, General Managers, Deputy General Managers, AGMs and other senior officers present on the occasion. Divisional, Zonal, and Cluster heads, along with other staff members, also participated in the ceremony virtually. Speaking on the occasion, Executive Director Sudhir Gupta said, “Public trust is the foundation of banking, and integrity is essential to preserving that trust as we grow. Our pursuit of sustainable growth must be supported by transparent processes, fair decisions and accountability at every level.” “Preventive vigilance must be part of our everyday work. Every employee has a responsibility to safeguard the Bank’s resources, protect customers’ interests and ensure that our conduct reflects the confidence people place in us. Let this pledge translate into consistent action throughout the year,” he added. Through the pledge, participants committed themselves to promoting ethical business practices, neither offering nor accepting bribes, and upholding corporate governance based on transparency, accountability and fairness. The pledge also emphasised adherence to relevant laws and compliance mechanisms, employee awareness of ethical responsibilities, grievance redressal and whistle-blower mechanisms for reporting fraudulent activities, besides protecting the rights and interests of stakeholders and society at large. Earlier, Chief Vigilance Officer Bansi Lal Saini stressed that building an organisation-wide culture of vigilance relies on the small, daily decisions of employees. These actions, he noted, are vital to deepening stakeholder trust in the institution. He urged participants to adopt three core principles: stay alert to their surroundings, take responsibility for their actions, and speak up when something goes wrong. The function concluded with a vote of thanks by General Manager (Vigilance) Hafeeza Rahim. “Our pledge must guide us throughout the year. By doing our work honestly and responsibly, we serve our customers better, protect our Bank and contribute meaningfully to its continued progress”, she said. Outlining the activities planned within the organisation during the week, she said that the Integrity Pledge would reinforce individual commitment, while the online quiz and essay competition would deepen awareness, help identify knowledge gaps and encourage ideas for improving ethical practices at the workplace.

in.title: Firmable breaks into G2's global top five for momentum in Sales Intelligence
in.description: Firmable earned 17 badges in G2's Fall 2026 reports and improved its ranking in 28 of the 32 reports it featured in last season, holding its position in the other four. MELBOURNE, Australia and SAN FRANCISCO, Oct. 28, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Firmable, the AI-native B2B sales platform, has climbed from #8 to #4 on G2's global Momentum Grid for Sales Intelligence, which ranks the fastest-rising products in the category worldwide. It also ranked #1 for SMB sales intelligence in both Australia and ANZ and moved into the top 10 across Asia-Pacific. Tech intelligence from Firmable is the new technographics The results span regional, segment and global reports in both the Sales Intelligence and Lead Intelligence categories. They are based on verified reviews from Firmable customers, alongside G2's measures of market presence and growth. Global momentum as Firmable scales in North America Firmable is now one of the fastest-rising sales intelligence products worldwide. Its jump to #4 on G2's global Momentum Grid for Sales Intelligence was matched by strong gains in G2's global satisfaction indexes: Relationship Index for Sales Intelligence: #3, up from #24 Implementation Index for Sales Intelligence: #3, up from #17 Results Index for Sales Intelligence: #4, up from #16 The results arrive as Firmable expands across the US and Canada, following its $14 million Series A in March and the launch of the Firmable MCP in July. They were followed by the launch of Tech Intelligence earlier in October. "G2 rankings come straight from customers, and that's why these results matter to us," said Leigh Jasper, co-founder and co-CEO of Firmable. "Customers are telling the market three things: Firmable is easy to work with, fast to roll out, and it delivers results. Those scores climbed the most this season. That's exactly the proof point sales leaders look for when they evaluate a new platform. We built Firmable as an AI-native product from day one, and teams in North America and elsewhere are responding. Breaking into the global top five for momentum is a strong signal of where we're headed." #1 in Australia and in ANZ Firmable took the top spot for small-business sales intelligence in both of its home markets. It rose from #2 to #1 on G2's Small-Business Australia Regional Grid for Sales Intelligence, and from #3 to #1 on the Small-Business ANZ Regional Grid. Firmable also held #1 overall in both Australia and ANZ for Lead Intelligence. "Ranking top in Australia and ANZ and climbing across Asia-Pacific comes down to one thing: our customers are booking more meetings with less effort," said Paul Perrett, co-founder and co-CEO of Firmable. "Growing sales teams can't afford to waste a rep's day on bad data or cold accounts. We give them verified contacts and buying signals that tell them who to call and when. These results show that approach is working for teams in every market we serve. And with the launch of Tech Intelligence last week, we're not slowing down." Top 10 across Asia-Pacific Firmable moved into the top 10 for small-business sales intelligence across Asia-Pacific. It climbed from #13 to #10 on G2's Small-Business Asia Pacific Regional Grid for Sales Intelligence. It also rose from #14 to #9 on the matching Lead Intelligence grid. Firmable debuted on G2's Mid-Market Asia Pacific Regional Grid for Sales Intelligence at #13. That reflects growing adoption among larger revenue teams in the region. On the overall Asia Pacific grid for Sales Intelligence, Firmable moved from #18 to #15. About G2 G2 is the world's largest and most trusted software marketplace. More than 90 million people annually use G2 to make smarter software decisions based on authentic peer reviews. Combining verified company and contact data with technology intelligence, CRM context, buyer intent and agentic AI, Firmable powers go-to-market teams across the US, Canada and Asia-Pacific. bd.title: 85% of Australians Would Switch Retailers if AI Finds a Better Deal this Peak Shopping Season
bd.description: New Manhattan Associates research reveals how AI could challenge retailer loyalty, with stock availability and fulfilment also influencing where shoppers buy SYDNEY, Oct. 28, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Australian retailers could face growing pressure to win over price-conscious shoppers this Black Friday and Christmas shopping period, with 85% of Australians willing to switch retailers if artificial intelligence (AI) found the same product for a better price elsewhere, according to new research commissioned by supply chain and commerce technology leader Manhattan Associates Inc. (NASDAQ: MANH). The findings come after Australians spent a record $23.8 billion over the extended Black Friday shopping period last year, according to CommBank iQ, setting the stage for another competitive sales period. AI could put retailer loyalty to the test The survey of Australian consumers found that 83% expect AI to play a role in their shopping activities over the coming months. Finding the best deals or lowest prices (35%) and comparing products, brands or retailers (36%) were the two leading ways respondents expected to use the technology. With AI making it easier for shoppers to compare offers from different retailers, businesses could find themselves competing for customers who might previously have gone straight to their preferred brands or stores. However, while a lower price might attract a shopper's attention, it won't necessarily be enough to secure the purchase. "AI is giving consumers another way to compare retailers, and that could make it harder for businesses to rely on established customer loyalty. If a shopper can find the same product for less elsewhere, they may be more willing to consider a retailer they haven't purchased from before," said Raghav Sibal, Vice President APAC at Manhattan Associates. "But price is only one part of the purchasing decision. Retailers also need to make sure the product is available, the delivery options are convenient, and the overall experience gives customers confidence to complete their purchase." A better price doesn't guarantee a sale Despite their willingness to use AI to find better deals, most Australians are not prepared to take its recommendations at face value. Nearly eight in ten Australians (78%) said they would check an AI-recommended deal against a retailer's website or other sources before purchasing. Price accuracy was the biggest concern, with 52% saying they would be most likely to double-check whether the price or discount was correct, followed by product information and reviews (23%) and delivery times or costs (20%). Retailer websites and apps also remain important to the purchasing process. While 35% of Australians said they would be comfortable completing a purchase directly through an AI shopping assistant, more than half (53%) would prefer to complete the transaction directly with the retailer. Stock availability could influence where shoppers buy Beyond price, the research suggests that product availability and fulfilment could play an important role in determining which retailer consumers choose. When asked which factor should determine an AI recommendation between retailers offering the same product at the same price, nearby stock availability was the leading response (39%), ahead of free delivery (28%) and faster fulfilment (27%). Australians also appear willing to share information to help AI find products they can purchase locally. Three in four respondents (75%) said they would share their location with an AI shopping assistant to find nearby stock. "An AI recommendation might bring a customer to a retailer's website, but the retailer still needs to deliver on what that customer expects. If the price doesn't match, the product isn't available or the delivery timeframe isn't suitable, the customer can easily look elsewhere," said Sibal. "During peak shopping periods, retailers need accurate inventory information across their sales channels and flexible fulfilment options to meet changing customer demand. Getting these fundamentals right will be important to converting AI-driven interest into sales, regardless of where a customer begins their shopping journey." -ends- Methodology: Manhattan Associates surveyed 500 Australian consumers. pk.title: Burundi BVD Ebola preparedness - DREF Operational Update (MDRBI026), 27 October 2026
pk.description: Please refer to the attached file. Description of the Event Date of event 21-05-2026 What happened, where and when? On 15 May 2026, the Government of the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) officially declared an outbreak of Ebola Virus Disease (BVD) caused by the Bundibugyo strain in Ituri Province, in the northeastern part of the country. On the same day, the Republic of Uganda also declared an outbreak of the same Ebola strain, with the epicenter located in Ituri. In response to the evolving situation and the cross-border implications of the outbreak, the World Health Organization (WHO) subsequently recognized the event as a major public health concern due to its spread in border areas and the high risk of regional transmission. The Bundibugyo strain currently has no approved vaccine, increasing concerns among health authorities and humanitarian partners. Ebola Virus Disease is a severe and often fatal illness transmitted through direct contact with infected bodily fluids, contaminated materials, or infected animals. The disease can cause large outbreaks with significant mortality if not rapidly contained. As of the date the emergency plan of action was written (May 2026), the epidemiological situation is still critical. As of 20 October 2026, no confirmed cases of Ebola virus disease have been reported in Burundi, according to the information provided. On 16 October 2026, the Ministry of Public Health refuted reports of a suspected case at Prince Régent Charles Hospital in Bujumbura. The individual tested negative for Ebola and other viral haemorrhagic fevers. However, the regional epidemiological situation remains a concern. The Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), the epicentre of the ongoing outbreak involving the Bundibugyo virus, continues to report cases and deaths. According to the figures cited in the available information, the World Health Organization (WHO) reported 8,728 confirmed cases and 4,205 deaths as of 6 October 2026. The risk of cross-border transmission is heightened by reported cases in neighbouring countries. In Kenya, an imported case linked to the DRC was confirmed in early October, and the patient died on 5 October. Contact tracing and follow-up measures were initiated, with subsequent reports indicating additional positive cases among individuals identified through contact investigations. In Uganda, authorities reported that no active cases remained following the discharge of the last patient on 16 July 2026. Burundi is considered a high-risk country due to its geographical proximity to the affected areas and its strong social and economic links with both the DRC and Uganda. Particular concern exists along major travel and trade corridors connecting Burundi to affected areas, including the Bujumbura–Goma, Bujumbura–Kivu, Bujumbura-Nairobi, and Bujumbura–Entebbe routes, through both land and air transport. The provinces bordering the DRC, as well as major entry points and urban centers receiving travelers, are considered areas at heightened risk of disease importation. Recognizing the threat posed by the outbreak, the Government of Burundi, in collaboration with health partners including the Burundi Red Cross Society and the IFRC, finalized and validated a National Ebola Preparedness and Response Plan on 22 May 2026. Preparedness efforts remain ongoing as the outbreak continues to evolve in neighboring countries and the risk of importation into Burundi remains high.

ae.title: Ronin pitches itself to Abstract users and creators as Dec. 15 shutdown approaches
ae.description: In Brief:Ronin wants Abstract's users and creators to move over to its network before the Ethereum layer 2 goes dark on Dec. 15, 2026. Ronin is asking creators affected by the shutdown to share their work, and says a creator program update is coming for both current and new creators on the chain. Abstract had more than 400,000 users and 144-plus apps. L2BEAT data shows about $48 million in assets still sat on the chain shortly before the shutdown was announced. Ronin is making a play for the users and creators of Abstract, the Ethereum layer 2 that Igloo Inc. plans to close on Dec. 15. In a post on X, Ronin wrote: "Abstract onboarded legions of people to our industry. If you're one of them, you may be wondering where to move your funds." Creators affected by this shutdown: we want to support you. Share your favorite piece of content below. A creator program update is on the way for current and new creators on Ronin.: https://creators.roninchain.com@RoninView on X ↗ The same post continued: "Bridge to Ronin and discover the home of Web3 gaming, AI-powered builders, and Axie Infinity (official site)."Creator program updateRonin then posted a follow-up aimed squarely at creators."Creators affected by this shutdown: we want to support you," the network wrote. "Share your favorite piece of content below."It added that "a creator program update is on the way for current and new creators on Ronin," with a link to creators.roninchain.com. Ronin gave no date for the update and no details on what it would change. Abstract's deadlineAbstract revealed the closure on X on Oct. 6, close to three years after development on the chain started. Operations end Dec. 15, 2026. Assets can be moved through the Migration Hub at migrate.abs.xyz or through the native bridge at native-bridge.abs.xyz, where transfers take roughly three hours."Any users that do not migrate their assets by this date will lose access to their funds," the project warned. No extension has been announced. Abstract has also told users to ignore impersonation attempts and unofficial migration links. During the wind-down, the team said, it will help third-party apps move to other networks. Why Igloo is pulling the plugAccording to Abstract, a chain focused solely on consumer crypto couldn't keep itself going. It cited thin liquidity, a limited DeFi ecosystem, weak institutional crossover and a smaller budget than its rivals. Luca Netz, Igloo's CEO, said the company had bankrolled Abstract for the past 18 months and lost "tens of millions of dollars" in the process. Igloo won't launch an Abstract token to keep the chain alive. Its resources are shifting to Pudgy Penguins, the Pudgy NFTs and PENGU.What's leaving the chainOver its run, Abstract brought on more than 400,000 users and over 144 applications, and it handled more than 300 million transactions. Disney and Red Bull Racing were both on the chain. Some of Abstract's games are moving their assets to Ethereum mainnet or to other networks ahead of the cutoff. Anyone who never bridged assets to Abstract is unaffected. Ronin's own wind-downRonin's pitch comes as it closes one of its own products. The Waypoint keyless wallet shuts down permanently when its final grace period expires at 15:00 UTC on Oct. 31, 2026. Only users who had already flagged migration problems on X, Discord or through a support ticket are covered by that grace period.

ae.title: 85% of Australians Would Switch Retailers if AI Finds a Better Deal this Peak Shopping Season
ae.description: New Manhattan Associates research reveals how AI could challenge retailer loyalty, with stock availability and fulfilment also influencing where shoppers buy SYDNEY, Oct. 28, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Australian retailers could face growing pressure to win over price-conscious shoppers this Black Friday and Christmas shopping period, with 85% of Australians willing to switch retailers if artificial intelligence (AI) found the same product for a better price elsewhere, according to new research commissioned by supply chain and commerce technology leader Manhattan Associates Inc. (NASDAQ: MANH). The findings come after Australians spent a record $23.8 billion over the extended Black Friday shopping period last year, according to CommBank iQ, setting the stage for another competitive sales period. AI could put retailer loyalty to the test The survey of Australian consumers found that 83% expect AI to play a role in their shopping activities over the coming months. Finding the best deals or lowest prices (35%) and comparing products, brands or retailers (36%) were the two leading ways respondents expected to use the technology. With AI making it easier for shoppers to compare offers from different retailers, businesses could find themselves competing for customers who might previously have gone straight to their preferred brands or stores. However, while a lower price might attract a shopper's attention, it won't necessarily be enough to secure the purchase. "AI is giving consumers another way to compare retailers, and that could make it harder for businesses to rely on established customer loyalty. If a shopper can find the same product for less elsewhere, they may be more willing to consider a retailer they haven't purchased from before," said Raghav Sibal, Vice President APAC at Manhattan Associates. "But price is only one part of the purchasing decision. Retailers also need to make sure the product is available, the delivery options are convenient, and the overall experience gives customers confidence to complete their purchase." A better price doesn't guarantee a sale Despite their willingness to use AI to find better deals, most Australians are not prepared to take its recommendations at face value. Nearly eight in ten Australians (78%) said they would check an AI-recommended deal against a retailer's website or other sources before purchasing. Price accuracy was the biggest concern, with 52% saying they would be most likely to double-check whether the price or discount was correct, followed by product information and reviews (23%) and delivery times or costs (20%). Retailer websites and apps also remain important to the purchasing process. While 35% of Australians said they would be comfortable completing a purchase directly through an AI shopping assistant, more than half (53%) would prefer to complete the transaction directly with the retailer. Stock availability could influence where shoppers buy Beyond price, the research suggests that product availability and fulfilment could play an important role in determining which retailer consumers choose. When asked which factor should determine an AI recommendation between retailers offering the same product at the same price, nearby stock availability was the leading response (39%), ahead of free delivery (28%) and faster fulfilment (27%). Australians also appear willing to share information to help AI find products they can purchase locally. Three in four respondents (75%) said they would share their location with an AI shopping assistant to find nearby stock. "An AI recommendation might bring a customer to a retailer's website, but the retailer still needs to deliver on what that customer expects. If the price doesn't match, the product isn't available or the delivery timeframe isn't suitable, the customer can easily look elsewhere," said Sibal. "During peak shopping periods, retailers need accurate inventory information across their sales channels and flexible fulfilment options to meet changing customer demand. Getting these fundamentals right will be important to converting AI-driven interest into sales, regardless of where a customer begins their shopping journey." -ends- Methodology: Manhattan Associates surveyed 500 Australian consumers. ae.title: Riverchain Secures US$10 Million Funding Commitment from dLab Asset Management to Scale Working Capital for Construction Contractors
ae.description: Commitment from a Hong Kong-based, SFC-licensed, technology-driven investment manager strengthens funding capacity on Riverchain's platform and reinforces its origination-as-a-service model. HONG KONG, Oct. 28, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Riverchain International Limited ("Riverchain" or the "Company"), a Hong Kong-based fintech specialising in working capital solutions for the construction industry, today announced that it has secured a US$10 million funding commitment from dLab Asset Management ("dLab"), a technology-driven investment manager specialising in data-driven SME financing across Asia Pacific. Riverchain Secures US$10 Million Funding Commitment from dLab Asset Management to Scale Working Capital for Construction Contractors The commitment significantly expands the funding capacity of Riverchain's platform as the Company continues to scale. Riverchain will originate working capital assets purpose-built for the construction sector, which dLab's commitment will fund. This enables more contractors and subcontractors to access timely financing that is structured around the realities of project cash flow. A partnership anchored in shared conviction The agreement pairs Riverchain's origination-as-a-service (OaaS) solution with an investment partner committed to long-term value creation. Riverchain sources, underwrites and services construction receivables, drawing on its proprietary technology and deep sector expertise. In turn, institutional partners such as dLab gain access to a high-quality, specialised asset class. dLab's strategy centres on financing SMEs through digital platforms, using data rather than company size to guide investment decisions across a diversified portfolio. Riverchain provides that platform for the construction sector. It originates and underwrites short-duration construction receivables using proprietary project and payment data, giving dLab direct access to an asset class that traditional lenders have historically underserved. Ben Wong, Founder and CEO of Riverchain, said: "We are proud to welcome dLab as a funding partner. dLab is a sophisticated investor with a long-term perspective and a vision closely aligned with our own. The backing of a partner of this calibre is a strong endorsement of our origination-as-a-service solution, our capabilities and the opportunity ahead. This commitment enhances our capacity to support Hong Kong's contractors as we continue to scale." Hiro Takaku, CEO of dLab Asset Management, said: "We believe that access to working capital should be driven by the quality of underlying business transactions, rather than the size of a company. Riverchain combines deep construction industry expertise with technology-driven origination and underwriting capabilities, making it a natural partner for dLab's Data-Based Finance strategy. Together, we aim to channel more institutional capital into an underserved but essential sector of Hong Kong's economy." About Riverchain International Limited Riverchain is a trusted provider of working capital solutions tailored to the construction industry. Combining proprietary technology with deep industry expertise, Riverchain simplifies access to financing and empowers construction companies to grow and succeed. Its offerings include bespoke and competitively priced factoring solutions, invoice financing and cash-flow-based loans. Beyond financing, Riverchain delivers value-added digital solutions and works with technology partners to enhance supply chain transparency across the built environment. Headquartered in Hong Kong, Riverchain serves clients across Hong Kong and Southeast Asia. About dLab Asset Management Limited dLab Asset Management ("dLab") is a Hong Kong-based investment manager licensed by the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) for Type 4 and Type 9 regulated activities (CE No. AZN664). Through its proprietary "Data-Based Finance" approach, dLab provides working capital financing to SMEs globally. Leveraging technology-driven origination platforms and transaction-level data, dLab manages diversified portfolios of short-duration receivables and trade finance assets for professional investors. ae.title: Farming Season cracks down on bots, freezing 5,578 farms and recycling 7.2 million SEASON into its reward pool
ae.description: In Brief:Farming Season (official site) announced on Oct. 27 that 5,578 farms have been frozen for cheating, with bot networks accounting for most of them. According to the team, 7,235,809 SEASON taken from frozen balances is already back in the reward pool, and roughly 2 million more will be added over the coming days. Every SEASON reward comes out of a single shared pool, so each cheating farm pulls rewards away from people who play by hand. In an Oct. 27 post on X, the Farming Season team said it had frozen 5,578 farms for cheating and moved 7,235,809 SEASON from their balances back into the game's reward pool. Roughly 2 million additional SEASON is "to be added to the reward pool in the coming days," according to the team. What are we doing to protect Farming Season? Every day, people try to cheat their way into the reward pool. Bots, scripts, fake results. Most players never see it. You should. Here's what happened behind the scenes, in real numbers 5,578 cheating farms frozen. 7.2Farming SeasonView on X ↗ "Every day, people try to cheat their way into the reward pool. Bots, scripts, fake results. Most players never see it," the team wrote. Bot networks account for most frozen farmsOf the frozen farms, 4,801 belonged to bot networks. The team described them as "Farms opened in batches and run in sync by one operator. Not players, factories."Forged results led to 499 more freezes. Those cases involved "Fake battle results, sped-up runs, loot no real run could ever earn," per the team. The remaining 278 farms were frozen over scripts and modified game code. According to the team, that group covered "Auto-clickers, dodge tools, macros and edited game code in the arena."Frozen balances return to the pool after 48 hoursFreezing a farm does more than shut it down. The team said the farm's balance is moved into the reward pool 48 hours after the freeze, "the same pool every honest farmer's rewards are paid from."Under the player guide, a frozen farm that isn't reopened inside that 48-hour window loses its balance to the pool."Every bot we catch doesn't just stop draining the pool. It refills it," the team said. The team linked the crackdown to a new pool balancer. The post announced the balancer but gave no details on how it works. "Together with the new pool balancer, this is how we keep the reward pool alive for the long run. Cheaters take from everyone. We give it back to the people who actually play," the team said. Fair-play rulesOn automation, the guide doesn't mince words: "Scripts, bots or macros running farms get them frozen." Players are allowed to run more than one farm, as long as every one of them is played by hand. According to the guide, "Everything is checked on the server." Harvests, timers, purchases and battle results all go through that check, and the team says this is how it spots modified clients and forged arena runs. Town Hall level sets the earnings cap, which runs from $1.50 a day at level 1 to about $40 at level 5. Withdrawal limits climb with level too and reset at 00:00 UTC.Pool economicsThe game recently reworked how in-game spending is divided. The reward pool's share went from 50% to 75%, while the burn share dropped from 50% to 25%. The guide says the 25/75 split applies to in-game spending as well as marketplace and bank fees, and all energy purchases go to the pool. Prior to the change, 255,199,250 SEASON, or 25.52% of supply, had been burned and verified on-chain, the team said. BackgroundSeason 1 opened at 16:00 UTC on Oct. 19, the same moment the SEASON token contract went live on Robinhood Chain. New players pay a one-time entry fee worth $1 in ETH on Robinhood Chain. The team wrote in an Oct. 26 post: "In just two weeks, 20,000 farms have been planting, crafting, fighting in the Battle Arena and racing in the Arena Cup." The Arena Cup carries a $3,000 weekly prize pool, and the game also pays out a daily $500 creator pool in SEASON.The anti-cheat post closed with a brief message to players: "Play by hand, play fair, keep farming."

Nous apportons l’argent, c’est à vous de travailler », a-t-il déclaré hier à Mandroseza, lors de la cérémonie de remise de douze camions-citernes pour renforcer la réponse aux besoins urgents après les cyclones Gezani et Fytia, dans le cadre du Projet d’amélioration de l’accès à l’eau potable (PAAEP), financé par la Banque mondiale. Le président de la Refondation de la République de Madagascar a annoncé que la présidence avait accordé à la société des subventions d’un millier de milliards d’ariary depuis l’avènement de ce régime. « (…) Il est surprenant de constater que la situation ne change toujours pas », a-t-il indiqué. Selon lui, 75 %, voire 85 %, de cette somme sont utilisés pour l’électricité, ce qui devrait permettre de régler le problème des coupures de courant. Mais sur le terrain, le délestage persiste. Hier, la Jirama a annoncé un délestage de deux heures aux heures de pointe sur le réseau interconnecté d’Antananarivo (RIA). Énergies renouvelables Selon les explications fournies, un déficit de 22 MW à la suite de la panne des machines de la turbine à combustion (TAC) 1, à Ambohimanambola, et la baisse du niveau d’eau à Andekaleka sont les deux facteurs de ce délestage. S’adressant aux employés de la Jirama, le chef de l’État a joué sur le registre moral : « Cela ne nous fait-il pas de peine de voir le peuple souffrir et se plaindre des coupures de courant ? La situation actuelle est-elle digne de la capitale du pays ? Posons-nous cette question. » Le directeur général, le général Hajatiana Rasolomanana, a donné ses explications à l’issue de la cérémonie. Le secteur de l’électricité serait celui qui engendre le plus de dépenses. « L’électricité génère de gros revenus, mais le carburant et les achats d’électricité auprès du privé pèsent lourdement sur les finances de l’entreprise », admet-il. La Jirama affiche l’ambition de gagner en autonomie et entend réduire peu à peu sa dépendance aux producteurs privés d’électricité et aux carburants coûteux, qui alourdissent ses charges. « Rappelez-vous toutefois que 20 % seulement de la population bénéficie de l’électricité de la Jirama. L’essentiel n’est pas d’écarter le privé, mais d’accroître la production, et nous veillerons à ce que ce soit la Jirama qui réalise cette augmentation. Les subventions allouées à la Jirama seront orientées vers l’investissement, pour construire des infrastructures propres à l’entreprise », a-t-il enchaîné. L’entreprise misera davantage sur les énergies renouvelables, en particulier le solaire, avec plusieurs projets en cours. Les centrales solaires de Mangatany, d’Ambatomirahavavy, d’Ilafy et d’Ampangabe font partie des projets réalisés ou en cours. Le directeur général de la Jirama s’est aussi adressé aux acteurs privés. « Nous ne vous demandons pas de faire œuvre de charité, mais de faire correctement votre travail, sans étouffer la Jirama. Si le privé prospère et que la Jirama s’appauvrit, c’est inacceptable, et ces contrats devront être annulés ou corrigés afin que la population bénéficie d’une électricité et d’une eau de qualité », a-t-il indiqué, en insistant sur l’importance d’une situation gagnant-gagnant. Le directeur général de la Jirama a aussi lancé un appel aux citoyens pour protéger les infrastructures de l’entreprise, victimes de vols et de dégradations. Ces pertes s’ajouteraient à celles liées à la vente d’électricité à un prix inférieur au coût de production. Miangaly Ralitera

mg.title: HUMOUR - Honorat sur le chemin du retour à la maison
mg.description: Évacué d’urgence vers l’Inde en avril, l’humoriste Honorat poursuit sa convalescence après une intervention chirurgicale au cœur. Selon son fils, il devrait rentrer à Madagascar cette semaine. Le retour de Honorat à Madagascar se précise. Après plusieurs mois de soins en Inde, où il a subi une opération du cœur, l’humoriste est désormais dans un état stable, selon son fils. Il poursuit toutefois son traitement et ses séances de rééducation. « L’opération est terminée. Il est actuellement en pleine convalescence et suit les traitements nécessaires avec les médicaments prescrits. On peut dire que son état est stable, mais il poursuit encore sa rééducation. Il devrait rentrer au pays cette semaine », a indiqué son fils. Une évacuation sanitaire en urgence Cette amélioration marque une étape dans son rétablissement, après plusieurs mois d’inquiétude pour ses proches. Son retour au pays ne signifie cependant pas la fin de sa prise en charge : les soins et la rééducation doivent se poursuivre. En avril, l’état de santé de Honorat s’était fortement dégradé. Selon les informations rapportées à l’époque, la partie inférieure de son corps ne réagissait plus. Son état avait nécessité une évacuation sanitaire vers l’Inde afin qu’il puisse bénéficier de soins adaptés. Son épouse l’avait accompagné, ainsi qu’un médecin chargé d’assurer son suivi médical durant le déplacement. Aujourd’hui, sa famille prépare son retour à Madagascar. Si la convalescence se poursuit, la stabilisation de son état, rapportée par son fils, est une évolution encourageante. Cassie Ramiandrasoa
